title: Can AI sales analytics tell your reps who to call and what to offer?
description: Sales analytics for banks, credit unions and insurers: six methods in plain words, list prices, fair lending rules and how to test a call list.
verdict: Reps keep the relationships; the model ranks which accounts to call and what to offer[^1][^2].
Start from what customers already own: it predicts their next product better than anything else[^3][^4].
Keep a random group uncalled, or you will pay for sales that would have happened anyway[^5][^6].
Disparate treatment is still illegal under the 2026 Regulation B rule, so compliance reviews targeting first[^7][^8].
Reward conversations and fit, not product counts: sales quotas cost Wells Fargo a $100 million fine[^9][^10].

summary: Sales analytics turns sales data into decisions; at a bank, credit union or insurer, AI ranks who to call, what to offer and why[^11][^1]. Reps still choose who to call[^2][^13]. Clean customer data and a holdout test make or break it[^12][^6].
humanRole: The rep, relationship manager or licensed agent keeps it: they pick who to call from the top of the list, and can skip anyone[^2][^13]. Their logged outcomes train the next version[^4].
Compliance officer: approves the offer list, targeting fields and exclusions before launch, and keeps the sign-off on file. Examiners review the criteria used to pick who gets prescreened offers[^8].
Head of retail banking or sales: sets goals on conversations and fit, not product counts[^14]. Pays no incentive tied to products per customer without risk controls[^10].
Analyst or marketing lead: owns the list, the uncalled holdout group and the monthly lift report[^6][^15].
teamAfter: Reps call from the top of the list and spend less time on desk research, so more of their day goes to conversations[^1].
Same people, better calls: commercial banking relationship managers with an analytics workbench grew portfolios 9%, against 5% for a control group[^1].
Less desk time: those managers spent 90% less time on account planning and got 5 times more cross-sell ideas[^1].
Most firms use AI to help staff: of firms reporting AI task effects, 66% only augment and 2% saw AI-related employment fall[^16][^17].
New workflows and staff training are the most common changes firms make with AI, at about 15% each[^16].

example.input: Illustrative $400 million credit union, not a real one. Its tier averages 58.2 checking accounts per 100 members, against 66.0 above $1 billion[^18]. One vendor puts credit unions' average share of members' auto loans at 21.8%[^19].
example.output: A list of 200 members ranked for auto refinance, each with a reason, such as "$412 a month car payment to another lender". The rep picks who to call and what to offer. A random 10% stay uncalled to measure lift[^6].

tables.title: What are the six sales analytics methods, in plain words?
tables.intro: They are share of wallet, white space, propensity, next best action, churn prediction and lookalike models, each answering one question about a customer[^11][^1]. The model ranks; the rep decides.
headers: Bank, credit union or insurer example

rows.name: Share of wallet
cells: Of all the money a customer keeps or borrows everywhere, the share you hold[^20][^21].
In one study, a top credit union held 38.8% of its members' auto loans; a top bank held 5.6%[^22].
Asks about outside accounts in conversation. Treats one customer's estimate as a lead, not a fact[^23].

rows.name: White space analysis
cells: A grid of customers by products. Each empty cell is a product they could hold but don't[^24][^25].
An insurance agency ranks clients with missing coverages, called account rounding[^26][^2].
Checks the gap is real before offering. An empty cell is a question, not proof of demand[^27].

rows.name: Propensity model
cells: A score for how likely each customer is to take one product soon. What they already own is the strongest clue[^3].
A credit union scores each member for a second product from holdings, balances and transactions[^4].
Works the top of the list and logs each outcome, which becomes training data[^4].

rows.name: Next best action
cells: For one customer right now, the single most useful step: an offer, a service call, a save, or nothing[^1].
A banker's CRM (customer relationship management) system suggests a call after a credit inquiry or rate change (vendor's signals)[^28][^29].
Accepts, edits or dismisses each suggestion. Skipping is valid: some customers react badly to any offer[^5].

rows.name: Churn prediction
cells: A score for who is likely to leave, close accounts or let a policy lapse soon[^30][^31].
A bank flags customers likely to close checking; a life insurer flags policies likely to lapse[^30][^31].
Makes the save call and decides, within policy, if a fee waiver is justified. Agree what counts as leaving first[^32].

rows.name: Lookalike model
cells: Start from your best customers and find others who resemble them. It predicts resemblance, not intent[^33].
Fits internal lists and distributor accounts[^34]. Meta bars lookalikes in financial product ads[^35].
Treats lookalike prospects as cold leads. Compliance reviews the seed list for credit products[^36].

tables.title: What did published studies find?
tables.intro: They found real gains: relationship managers with analytics grew portfolios 9% against 5%, and a bank offer opened 82% more accounts than a control[^1][^42]. These are other teams' results; yours can differ, which is why you test.

rows.name: McKinsey, 2023
cells: Commercial banking relationship managers with an analytics workbench grew portfolios 9% in 12 months, against 5% for a control group[^1].

rows.name: Knott, Hayes and Neslin, 2002
cells: In a bank field test, a next-product-to-buy model beat a rule of thumb on profit. Current product ownership predicted best[^3].

rows.name: Harland Clarke case (vendor)
cells: At a $22 billion bank, a checking offer opened 82% more accounts than a same-propensity control group[^42].

rows.name: Portrait Software, 2006 (vendor)
cells: In bank cross-sell, an uplift model scored 19.03% on the vendor's measure, against 15.29% for the best response model[^15].

rows.name: Annals of Operations Research, 2023
cells: Adding transaction data to demographics raised AUC, a ranking-accuracy score, by 4 to 5.4 points[^43].

rows.name: Insurance: Mathematics and Economics, 2024
cells: For a Taiwan life insurer, XGBoost predicted lapses best. A two-stage model raised net present value[^31].

recipes.name: 1. Community bank or credit union: first call list on the CRM you own
recipes.when: You have a CRM or marketing customer file and one analyst. Start with two products, such as auto refinance and home equity, and read the result after 60 days[^4][^3].
flow: Data lead: export 24 months of holdings, balances and transactions from the core
Data lead: link accounts into households
Analyst: build the white-space grid and a propensity score for two products
Compliance officer: review targeting fields and the offer list, then sign off
Head of retail: set goals on conversations and outcomes, not product counts
Reps: call the top of the list, with the reason shown, and log each outcome
Analyst: compare against the 10% uncalled group after 60 days
recipes.cost: Use a CRM you own, or a listed one: HubSpot Sales Hub Pro is $90 a seat a month[^38]. Dynamics 365 Sales Premium is $150 a user a month[^29].

recipes.name: 2. Bank or credit union on a digital banking platform: bought module
recipes.when: You run Alkami or a similar platform and want campaigns plus scoring without a modelling team[^39]. Vendor models still need validation and outcomes checks[^44].
flow: Head of retail: pick the module tier
Vendor and data lead: connect core and digital banking data
Compliance officer: ask the vendor for its fair lending tests, the reason shown for each pick and its validation papers
Marketing lead and reps: run campaigns and calls from the list, keeping a holdout
Analyst: each quarter, check the lift and whether the scores still hold up
recipes.cost: Alkami lists $23,000, $47,000 or $77,000 a year by tier, read 26 Nov 2026[^39]. Data connection work is extra.

recipes.name: 3. Insurance agency: account rounding
recipes.when: An agency that wants each client's missing coverages ranked for producers[^26][^2]. Check your state's AI bulletin first[^45].
flow: Agency operations: connect the agency management system to a rounding tool
Producer: work the ranked list of missing coverages
Licensed agent: judge suitability before any offer
Agency principal: check state AI bulletin duties, such as Colorado's
Agency operations: track the rounding rate against an uncalled holdout
recipes.cost: AgencyKPI lists $250 a month, or $166.67 a month billed yearly, read 26 Nov 2026[^26]. OpSpring prices by credits and publishes no amounts[^2].

ownData.title: What do sales analytics vendors show on their own pages?
ownData.intro: Most show little you need to check: 2 of 9 publish a price, 1 names fair lending and 4 show a reason for each pick[^39][^28][^13]. We read the product or pricing pages of 9 sales analytics vendors on 26 Nov 2026[^46][^47][^48][^2][^26][^49]. Eight sell to banks, credit unions or insurance agencies; one sells to distributors.

ownData.note: Zavient check of vendor marketing pages on 26 Nov 2026, not contracts, documents or demos. A page silent on fairness doesn't mean the product lacks controls. Nine vendors from search results, one date, not a census.

rules.name: Regulation B final rule, 91 FR 21620
rules.what: Removes disparate-impact liability under the Equal Credit Opportunity Act (ECOA)[^7][^50]. Discouragement now covers words and images, not acts such as ad targeting[^7][^51]. Disparate treatment is still banned, and the Fair Housing Act and state laws still apply[^7][^36][^66][^67].

rules.name: Regulation B, 12 CFR 1002.4(b)
rules.what: You may not say things that would discourage people from applying on a prohibited basis[^52]. Marketing that encourages a group to apply is allowed[^52].

rules.name: CFPB ECOA exam procedures
rules.what: Examiners review marketing materials, prescreened offers and the criteria used to pick recipients[^8]. Keep your targeting fields and sign-off on file.

rules.name: CFPB Compliance Bulletin 2016-03, production incentives
rules.what: The CFPB's 2016 bulletin warned that sales goals and incentives can drive steering and unrealistic quotas[^53]. The same year, Wells Fargo paid a $100 million CFPB fine over about 1.5 million unauthorized accounts[^9]. New York's regulator warned against pay tied to products per customer without risk controls[^10].

rules.name: Regulation V, 12 CFR 1022.21, affiliate marketing
rules.what: Using an affiliate's data to market, such as insurance data to sell a home equity loan, needs notice and an opt-out[^54]. The opt-out lasts at least 5 years[^54].

rules.name: Regulation P, 12 CFR 1016.13
rules.what: Sharing customer data with an outside analytics firm or joint marketer needs a privacy notice[^55]. It also needs a contract limiting how the firm uses the data[^55].

rules.name: Federal Reserve SR 26-2 and OCC Bulletin 2026-13, model risk
rules.what: Aimed mainly at banks over $30 billion; for smaller banks and credit unions, treat it as best practice[^44]. It still expects an independent challenge of the model, checks on its results and validation of vendor models[^44]. Generative AI is out of scope[^44].

rules.name: NCUA guidance on artificial intelligence
rules.what: NCUA has not issued AI-specific rules; existing rules apply[^56]. Examiners look at due diligence on third-party vendors[^56].

rules.name: National Association of Insurance Commissioners (NAIC) AI Model Bulletin
rules.status: Adopted by about 27-28 states plus DC and Puerto Rico (map of 13 Nov 2026)
rules.what: Covers insurers' AI use, marketing included: governance, testing for unfair discrimination and vendor oversight[^57][^45]. Colorado adds its own testing rules for life, private auto and health insurers[^58].

howToTest: Pilot it on one product in one branch, keep part of the list uncalled, and compare take-up before you roll it out[^6]. Record today's numbers there first: contacts made, offers taken, balances opened and rep time per conversation.
Back-test: score last quarter's customers using data as of its first day. Check whether the top tenth really opened more products than the rest.
Keep a random 10% of the top of the list uncalled. Lift is the called group's take-up minus the uncalled group's[^6].
Also call a small random group below the cut-off. That tests the ranking itself, not just the calls[^15].
If many top-scored customers buy without a call, switch to uplift targeting: aim at people a call actually persuades[^59][^5].
For credit products, compare who gets picked and what they are offered across groups, and document the review[^8]. Insurers in Colorado must test for unfair discrimination[^58].
Price the lift: extra balances or premium times margin, minus rep time and tool cost, over 90 days.
Rescore monthly or quarterly. Propensity models need a periodic refresh[^60].
watchOuts: It goes wrong through quota abuse, lookalike and proxy bias, bad household data, chasing people who would buy anyway, and lists with no reasons[^9][^8]. Each fix is below.
Quotas built on model lists invite abuse: Wells Fargo staff opened about 1.5 million unauthorized deposit accounts[^9]. Reward conversations and fit, not product counts[^10][^14].
Lookalike seeds copy the seed list's makeup. Meta bars lookalikes for financial product ads, and HUD flags them for housing[^35][^36].
Targeting fields can stand in for a protected trait. Disparate treatment is still illegal, so compliance reviews each field before launch[^7][^8].
Poor householding hides customers, and many banks haven't linked accounts into households[^12]. Fix the data before you score it.
Response models chase people who would buy anyway, and some customers react badly to any contact[^5][^15]. Test with an uncalled group and consider uplift[^59].
A list with no reasons leaves reps unable to explain and compliance unable to review. Only 4 of the 9 vendor pages we checked showed a reason per pick[^13][^2].

faq.q: How do banks calculate share of wallet?
faq.a: Divide what a customer keeps or borrows with you by their total across all institutions[^21][^20]. US consumers hold about 8.5 banking products across institutions, so most wallets are split[^61][^62].

faq.q: What is the difference between a propensity model and an uplift model?
faq.a: A propensity model finds who is likely to buy, while an uplift model finds who buys because you called[^59]. Response models tend to target people who would have bought anyway[^5].

faq.q: Can banks use lookalike audiences on Facebook?
faq.a: Not for financial product ads, because Meta's special ad category for financial products and services bars lookalike audiences in the US[^35][^63].

faq.q: Does the 2026 Regulation B rule mean targeting is unrestricted?
faq.a: No: from 21 Jul 2026 it drops disparate-impact liability and limits discouragement to words and images[^7][^50]. Disparate treatment, the Fair Housing Act and state laws still apply[^7][^36][^66][^67].

faq.q: What does sales analytics software cost?
faq.a: CRM seats with AI scoring list at $90 to $150 a user a month[^38][^29]. Alkami's bank marketing module starts at $23,000 a year[^39]. Revenue intelligence tools such as Gong don't publish prices[^40][^41].

faq.q: Does sales analytics take over from our reps?
faq.a: No: it ranks the list, and reps still choose who to call and what to say[^2][^1]. Of firms reporting AI task effects, 66% use it only to help staff[^16].

buyVsBuild.buy: Mostly buy the scoring and workflow inside the CRM or digital banking platform you already run[^29][^39]. In one survey of enterprise buyers, 76% of AI use cases were bought rather than built[^64].
buyVsBuild.build: Build the parts that are yours: the household data join, the holdout test and the fair lending review[^12][^8]. Few vendor pages we checked show these[^28]. In MIT's study, outside partners reached deployment about twice as often as internal builds[^65].

pickElse: When you have few products or a small customer base: a spreadsheet white-space grid is enough to start[^24][^25].
Already on Salesforce Financial Services Cloud, Dynamics 365 Sales Premium or HubSpot Sales Hub Pro: turn on the built-in scoring first[^29][^38].
Insurance agency: try a rounding tool such as AgencyKPI before a custom model[^26].
Need to forecast the pipeline, not pick accounts: revenue intelligence tools such as Gong or Clari fit better[^40][^41].

offer.heading: Get a ranked call list your compliance officer can sign off on
offer.body: Bring us your sales analytics process: your core, CRM or policy data and how reps work today. In 30 minutes you leave with the first product and branch to pilot, and a before-and-after measure. You get it in writing, with no sales pitch.

reviews.notes: Dana wanted the first process, the measure and something to forward. On this page now links the three builds, each with a role on every step. Recipe 1 names two first products and when to read the result: 60 days, against the uncalled group.

Tripped on drift, reason codes, effective challenge and outcomes analysis. Each is now in plain words: whether scores still hold up, the reason shown for each pick, an independent challenge of the model, checks on its results.

Asked whether one unit can pilot first and what it does to margin. The first test step now pilots one product in one branch or region. The pricing step already turns lift into dollars net of rep time and tool cost.

Head of retail banking checked the roles against the exam procedures and the incentive lessons. Compliance now keeps its sign-off on file for examiners. The head of retail now owns pay rules: no incentive tied to products per customer without risk controls. Next best action example now uses a banker, not a loan officer.

Gets the answer from the title and five short bullets. Would distrust a commercial-banking result passed off as retail, so the McKinsey figure now says commercial banking relationship managers everywhere. Offer now promises the first product and branch to pilot. External list prices are shown; no Zavient price is set, so none is shown.

answers.table-1: The six are share of wallet, white space analysis, propensity models, next best action, churn prediction and lookalike models, each answering one question about a customer[^11][^1].
answers.table-2: CRM seats list at $65 to $700 a user a month, Alkami's bank data module at $23,000 to $77,000 a year, and an agency rounding tool at $250 a month[^29][^37][^39][^26].
answers.table-3: Studies found analytics helps: relationship managers with an analytics workbench grew portfolios 9% against 5% for a control group, and a next-product model beat a rule of thumb[^1][^3].
answers.own-data: Of the 9 vendor pages we read, only 2 publish a price, 1 names fair lending, and 4 show a reason for each pick[^39][^26][^28][^13].
answers.human-role: The rep or licensed agent keeps the decision and can skip anyone, while compliance signs off targeting and the sales head sets goals on conversations and fit[^2][^8][^14].
answers.team-after: Reps still pick who to call and what to offer, but spend less time on account planning and get more cross-sell ideas to bring to each conversation[^2][^1].
answers.example: At an illustrative $400 million credit union, the model ranks 200 members for auto refinance with a reason for each, and reps choose who to call[^6].
answers.recipes: Community banks and credit unions start with a call list on their own CRM, digital banking platform users buy a module, and insurance agencies use a rounding tool[^4][^39][^26].
answers.rules: Regulation B's fair-lending rules apply, along with CFPB exam procedures, privacy and affiliate-marketing rules (Regulations P and V), model-risk guidance, and the NAIC AI bulletin for insurers[^7][^8][^55][^54][^44][^57].
answers.benchmark: Pilot one product in one branch, back-test the scores on last quarter, keep a random 10% uncalled to measure lift, and price the gain over 90 days[^6].
answers.what-goes-wrong: Sales analytics fails when quotas on model lists invite abuse, targeting fields stand in for protected traits, household data is messy, or lists chase people who'd buy anyway[^9][^7][^12][^5].
answers.something-else: Pick something else when a spreadsheet grid is enough, your CRM already has built-in scoring, an agency can start with a rounding tool, or you need pipeline forecasting instead[^24][^29][^26][^40].
